## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Saṁsaṭṭhā* (“Inappropriate socializing”) is the twelfth rule in the *Saṅghādisesa* section of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule addresses communal disharmony among nuns, prescribing suspension for nuns who persistently engage in notorious, inappropriate socialization, cause trouble for the monastic community, and conceal each other's disciplinary offenses. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Computational reuse analyses by DharmaNexus demonstrate extensive shared formulary phrasing across 94 Pali texts, with the closest affinities found in adjacent disciplinary rules such as *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa* 13, 10, and 11, *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa* 10–13, the *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* (Kd 20), and subcommentarial treatises [DharmaNexus].
